newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: New members named to CSFB's board.
newsitem.headline: New members named to CSFB's board.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB) said its shareholders approved the appointment of Mario Corti, general manager of chocolate and foods group Nestle AG and Ernst Tanner, chief executive of chocolate manufacturer Lindt and Spruengli AG to its board.
Credit Suisse Group carried out a major restructuring last year aimed at internationalising and streamlining its business.

As part of the move, activities were brought into four main divisions, which include investment banking under CSFB, domestic banking under the Credit Suisse brand, Credit Suisse Private Banking and Credit Suisse asset management.
The latest appointments were made to ensure that no-one holds multiple directorships at Credit Suisse Group, CSFB said.
Ulrich Bremi and Heini Lippuner were also re-elected as members of CSFB's board of directors.
Helmust Maucher, who is stepping down as chief executive of Nestle in June, and Robert Jeker, chairman of Swiss steel firm von Moos have stepped down from CSFB's board.
Lukas Muhlemann took on the post of Group chief executive January 1, while Rainer Gut remains chairman of the board. Gut is also chairman of CSFB's board.
